title: Pingu-Slide 🐧 My First AI Project and a Little Story Behind It
author: suspicious-night-owl
selftext:
To enjoy the full potential, **please look the video with sounds on** :)

This game started as a spontaneous idea I had while playing with my godchild.

We were lying on the floor on a blanket, playing with little animal figurines. Since penguins are among his favorite animals, the idea for this game came to me.



I'm actually not much of an AI user when it comes to programming.

I've been coding since I was 12 years old (back then only with HTML and JavaScript), and I'm now in my late 30s, so many of you can probably already guess why.

**I have absolutely nothing against using AI for coding. Personally, I just enjoy knowing every little detail of the code I'm working with.**

Even I still don't use AI coding for my larger projects, I thought this little minigame would be a great opportunity to give it a try!



So I had a rather **long getting-to-know-you date** with Open Code and GLM-5.3 Flash.

We spent around 8 hours together. While my date was talking to itself, I used the time to get other things done.

This was not even close a "one-prompt" project! The textures, logo and sounds weren't created by GLM either.

But I have to say, all in all, it was a cool and relatively fast process.

What surprised me the most was its ability to detect its own mistakes and work through correction loops.



**More details** for anyone curious about how this was made:  
Coding: Open Code + GLM-5.3 Flash (free version)  
Textures + Logo: Qwen Image Edit 2.1 Turbo  
Sounds: Pixabay



**I'd really appreciate your feedback!**

First, I'd love to hear your thoughts on the game idea itself and its current state, which you can see in the video.

I'd also be interested in hearing about your experiences with GLM-5.3 Flash or other free alternatives.



**And if you're interested in more than just AI, feel free to follow me on Reddit or YouTube.**

You'll also get to see my other game there, which, in contrast to this one, is being developed with 0% AI involvement.



I think it's important that we don't limit ourselves to rigid categories or put everything into boxes.

If someone likes AI and wants to work with it → go for it! There's nothing wrong with that!

If someone thinks AI sucks and doesn't want anything to do with it → go for it! There's nothing wrong with that either!
